claim: A Copper WAIT matches its line only for equality (the position is at-or-past), so a WAIT for a line the beam has passed holds until the next frame; and the Copper counts the left border of line n + 1 as line n.
limit: The passed-line hold and copper line = raster line measured on the N-Go board (Issue 2-compatible clone, core 3.03.00, nxsuite P01, P04); the left-border count and the h limits (55 on a 456-dot line, 54 on 448) are from the book.

evidence.source: I. Novak, Unraveling the ZX Spectrum Next, Vol 1 (2026; core 3.03.03), chapter 18
evidence.text: The Copper's horizontal count starts 12 dots before the display area and its line number moves on there, so dot 408 of line 99 is the left edge of line 100's border; a list whose WAITs are out of line order stalls for a frame.
N-Go board (Issue 2-compatible clone), core 3.03.00 (nxsuite P01): a WAIT for a line already passed held the rest of the list until that line in the next frame.
N-Go board (Issue 2-compatible clone), core 3.03.00 (nxsuite P04): copper WAITs for lines 0, 120, 191 and 250 matched the same $1E/$1F raster lines.
